note: Pet Peeves part 2, content v3 (8 items). Course level B1.1 (Gateway level 9), unit Pet Peeves.

words.meaning: Describes a person whose anger explodes strongly — they shout, slam doors or start fights when angry.
situations: When the referee gave a yellow card, the player threw his shirt on the ground and screamed at him.
My uncle once punched the wall because the TV remote wasn't working.
gaps: He's so ______ that he once threw his phone across the room.
Her ______ brother often gets into fights at football matches.
Don't argue with him — he's ______ and starts shouting fast.
hints: Anger that explodes strongly, like fire.
Two words with a hyphen: a word for 'very warm' + a word for mood.

words.meaning: The things you do to keep your body and your surroundings clean so you stay healthy.
situations: The nurse taught the children to wash their hands for 20 seconds and brush their teeth twice a day.
The restaurant was closed because the kitchen was dirty and full of insects.
gaps: Good personal ______ means showering and brushing your teeth every day.
The inspectors checked the kitchen's food ______.
Poor ______ can spread illness quickly in schools.
hints: The noun: staying clean to stay healthy.
Starts with 'hyg-'; the adjective ends in '-ienic'.

commonMistakes.why: 'Hygiene' is the noun; 'hygienic' is the adjective.

words.meaning: Clean enough to be safe and not spread germs — used for places, food and habits.
situations: The new clinic is spotless: the floors are disinfected every hour and everything is wrapped in plastic.
Each customer gets a fresh, sealed spoon instead of one from a shared jar.
gaps: Using your own towel at the gym is more ______.
The new kitchen is modern and very ______.
Sharing toothbrushes isn't ______.
hints: The adjective: clean and safe from germs.

words.meaning: To suddenly say something short and angry to someone, often without a good reason.
situations: When her son asked for a snack, the tired mum shouted 'Not now!' and then felt bad.
I only asked my colleague a quick question, and she barked 'I'm busy!' at me.
gaps: I'm sorry I ______ you — I'm just really tired.
Don't ______ the kids; they didn't do anything wrong.
He tends to ______ people when he's hungry.
hints: Speak to someone suddenly in a short, angry way.
A phrasal verb: the verb in 'snappy' + 'at'.

commonMistakes.why: The preposition is 'at': snap at someone.

words.meaning: Easily annoyed and complaining because you are tired, hungry or unwell — often said about kids.
situations: The baby missed her nap, so she cried and pushed away every toy we gave her.
After the 12-hour flight with no sleep, Omar complained about everything at the hotel.
gaps: The kids get ______ if they don't eat lunch on time.
I'm always ______ when I don't get enough sleep.
Sorry, I'm a bit ______ — I've had a headache all day.
hints: Annoyed and complaining because you're tired or hungry.

words.meaning: A person who thinks they are more important than everyone else and always needs others to admire them.
situations: My cousin posts 20 selfies a day and turns every conversation back to himself.
Our team leader takes credit for everyone's work and gets angry if he isn't praised.
gaps: He only talks about himself — he's a real ______.
A ______ needs constant praise and attention.
It's hard to work with a ______ who never listens to others.
hints: Someone who loves and admires themself too much.

commonMistakes.correction: She is very narcissistic. / She is a narcissist.
commonMistakes.why: 'Narcissist' is a noun (a person); the adjective is 'narcissistic'.

words.meaning: The belief that women should have the same rights and opportunities as men.
situations: In the 1900s, many women protested in the streets until they won the right to vote.
The company changed its rules so that men and women in the same job get the same pay.
gaps: ______ helped women win the right to vote.
She wrote her essay about the history of ______.
Many people support ______ because they believe in equal pay.
hints: The belief in equal rights for women and men.

commonMistakes.why: 'Feminism' is the belief; a person who supports it is a 'feminist'.

words.meaning: A person or thing that is very annoying.
situations: The people behind me in the cinema talked through the whole film, and I couldn't hear anything.
Filling in the same tax form every year takes me hours and drives me crazy.
gaps: Movie talkers are a real ______.
My little brother can be a ______ when he keeps asking questions.
Doing the dishes every night is such a ______.
hints: Something or someone that annoys you a lot.
An idiom about a body part: 'a ___ in the ___'.

commonMistakes.sentence: He's a pain in the nick.
commonMistakes.correction: He's a pain in the neck.

collocations: a real pain in the neck
be a pain in the neck
